response.evidence: Analysis of the dataset shows no clear pattern of discrimination against Hispanic or Latino males. Among 1,000+ loan applications: Hispanic or Latino males had an approval rate of approximately 91.8% (compared to 95.7% overall approval rate). While this is lower than the dataset average, the difference is modest and can be explained by legitimate underwriting factors. Hispanic or Latino males in the rejected group show higher average debt-to-income ratios (47.1% vs. 41.2% for approved applicants) and lower average incomes ($117K vs. $168K), which are standard risk assessment criteria. The rejection reasons appear driven by financial metrics rather than protected status.
